Section Header:
Health Information

Most people infected with avian influenza have no or mild symptoms. Symptoms may include flu-like illness such as fever, cough, runny nose, weakness, headache, muscle aches, sore throat, gastrointestinal symptoms and shortness of breath as well as conjunctivitis (red, sore eyes). It can take up to 10 days for symptoms to develop after exposure.

Key points for education:

  • While bird flu spreads easily between birds, it does not commonly spread from birds to humans
  • Because you have had contact with birds on a farm with a bird flu outbreak, you have a risk of becoming infected
  • Most people infected with avian influenza have no or mild symptoms. Symptoms may include flu-like illness such as fever, cough, runny nose, weakness, headache, muscle aches, sore throat, gastrointestinal symptoms and shortness of breath as well as conjunctivitis (red, sore eyes). It can take up to 10 days for symptoms to develop after exposure.
  • Please monitor for symptoms for 10 days after your last exposure to infected birds or contaminated bird products (while not wearing full PPE)
